name: Lercanidipine
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Lercanidipine is a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker cleared by CYP3A4 metabolism; levels are about 70% higher in severe kidney impairment and dialysis. Unlike amlodipine, the European label contraindicates it at glomerular filtration rate (GFR) below 30 mL/min, including dialysis, and asks for caution when increasing to 20 mg in mild to moderate impairment. In peritoneal dialysis it can cloud the effluent. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses glomerular filtration rate (GFR, mL/min) for the contraindication; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 10 mg once daily at least 15 minutes before a meal, preferably in the morning; may increase to 20 mg after about 2 weeks (SmPC).
Mild to moderate impairment: start with special care; 10 mg may be tolerated, but increase to 20 mg cautiously (SmPC).
Contraindicated: severe kidney impairment (GFR <30 mL/min), including dialysis (SmPC).

hd.text: Contraindicated in dialysis (SmPC). Use another calcium-channel blocker (e.g., amlodipine).

pd.text: Contraindicated in dialysis (SmPC). Can cause cloudy peritoneal effluent that mimics peritonitis.

dialyzable: No: dialysis is unlikely to help in overdose (over 98% protein-bound) (SmPC).
monitoring: Blood pressure; peripheral edema; heart rate. Avoid grapefruit, alcohol, strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and cyclosporine (contraindicated) (SmPC).
